comparisons.peer_summary: Operating expenses decreased 2% to $33.77 billion in 2024, aided by lower CIE commercial real estate impairments and prior year one-time charges like the GreenSky write-down, partially offset by higher compensation and transaction expenses, resulting in an efficiency ratio improvement to 63.1% from 74.6%.
comparisons.comparison: Both C and GS reported decreases in overall operating expenses for 2024, attributing the reductions to specific non-recurring or regulatory charges from the prior year. C stated expenses decreased 19% primarily due to lower FDIC expenses and reduced restructuring charges, partially offset by Consent Order costs. Similarly, GS reported operating expenses decreased 2%, driven by significantly lower expenses related to CIE impairments and prior year one-time charges like the GreenSky write-down and FDIC special assessment fee, partially offset by higher compensation.

sentences.text: Expenses decreased 19%, primarily driven by lower FDIC expenses ($203 million in 2024 versus approximately $1.7 billion in the prior year) and the reduction from the closed exits and wind-downs, as well as lower restructuring charges ($259 million in 2024 versus $781 million in the prior year), partially offset by the costs of the July 2024 Consent Orders entered into with the FRB and OCC.

Operating expenses were $33.77 billion for 2024, 2% lower than 2023, reflecting decreases driven by significantly lower expenses, including impairments, related to commercial real estate in consolidated investment entities (CIEs) and other significant expenses recognized in the prior year, including the write-down of identifiable intangible assets related to GreenSky Holdings, LLC (GreenSky), an impairment of goodwill related to Consumer platforms and the FDIC special assessment fee.

comparisons.peer_summary: Noninterest expense decreased 29% to $4.0 billion, driven by lower FDIC assessments, reduced First Republic-related costs, and lower legal expenses, partially offset by a $1.0 billion Visa share contribution to the JPMorgan Chase Foundation and higher international consumer initiative costs.
comparisons.comparison: Both C and JPM highlighted FDIC-related expenses as a key driver of expense reduction in 2024 compared to the prior year. C reported a decrease in expenses driven by lower FDIC expenses ($203 million vs $1.7 billion), while JPM reported a 29% decrease in noninterest expense driven by a lower FDIC special assessment. Both companies also noted partial offsets from other specific items; C cited costs from Consent Orders, while JPM cited higher international consumer initiative costs and a charitable contribution.
